quench.title: Quenching zone
quench.description: The element splits the flow into many narrow channels. A flame entering them loses heat to the metal walls faster than it can release it; it cools below its ignition temperature and is extinguished. The gap size is chosen for the gas group (MESG).

summary: A flame arrestor lets gas or vapour flow through but stops a flame from passing. Its element divides the flow into many very narrow channels; a flame entering them loses heat to the metal so fast that it is cooled below ignition and extinguished. In-line deflagration arrestors protect tanks, vent headers and burners against flashback.

fa_housing.function: Expands the pipe to the element diameter so flow velocity in the element stays low.
fa_housing.construction: Two flanged halves clamping the element.
fa_housing.operating_conditions: Pressure drop rises as element fouls.

fa_element.function: Quenches the flame in narrow channels.
fa_element.construction: Crimped and flat metal ribbons wound together forming triangular channels.
fa_element.operating_conditions: Must match gas group, temperature and installation distance from ignition source.
inspection: Inspect & clean; replace after a stabilised burn

pipework.function: Connects the pump to the system.
pipework.construction: Flanged pipe spools, fittings and supports; suction piping laid out to give uniform flow into the pump (straight run, eccentric reducers flat side up).
pipework.material: Carbon steel, stainless steel, ductile iron, HDPE/PVC as appropriate.
pipework.operating_conditions: Piping must be supported independently so nozzle loads stay within limits.
inspection: Check supports and flange alignment before bolting to pump

flow_tracers.construction: Small spheres moving along the main flow path during the Operate animation.
